changes.value: Adults 19+ without a qualifying immigration status can no longer newly enroll in full-scope Medi-Cal
changes.detail: Existing enrollees keep coverage if they renew on time. Children, pregnant people, and former foster youth under 26 are unaffected. Source: DHCS Medi-Cal Changes.

changes.item: January 1, 2026 — asset limits reinstated for non-MAGI programs
changes.value: $130,000 for one person, +$65,000 per additional person (up to 10)
changes.detail: Applies to people 65+, people with a disability, nursing home residents, and families over the MAGI income limit. MAGI-based Medi-Cal (adults 19–64) still has no asset test. This was restored by AB 116 (Chapter 21, Statutes of 2025) and implemented by DHCS. Source: DHCS asset-limit FAQ.

changes.item: January 1, 2026 — 2026 FPL figures effective for MAGI determinations
changes.detail: Effective January 1, 2026 for MAGI; April 1, 2026 for the Aged, Blind and Disabled FPL programs and the 250% Working Disabled Program. Source: DHCS ACWDL 26-01.

changes.item: October 2026 — federal reclassification of certain immigration statuses
changes.value: State-funded full-scope Medi-Cal until June 30, 2027 for affected groups
changes.detail: Refugees and asylees, humanitarian parolees, and certain survivors of domestic violence or trafficking with pending cases. From July 1, 2027: pregnancy-related care and emergency services only.

changes.item: October 1 – December 31, 2026 — work-rule notice in every application packet
changes.value: Counties must include the DHCS outreach letter with application materials
changes.detail: DHCS began mailing outreach notices to New Adult Group members in late August 2026. The notice explains the work rule, the six-month renewal rule, the exemptions, and the consequences of non-compliance.

changes.item: January 1, 2027 — work and community engagement requirements begin
changes.value: 80 hours/month, or $580 monthly income, or an exemption or short-term hardship
changes.detail: Applies to the MAGI New Adult Group in California, regardless of immigration status. Applications dated on or before December 31, 2026 are not assessed for the work rule until the member's next renewal in 2027.

changes.value: Redetermination every 6 months instead of 12, for the MAGI New Adult Group
changes.detail: Section 71107 of H.R. 1. Members are moved from an annual to a six-month cycle at the same time the work rule starts. Tribal members, pregnant/postpartum members, and children are not subject.

changes.value: Undocumented people, some green card holders in the five-year bar, and PRUCOL residents move to FFS
changes.detail: This changes how you get care, not whether you keep Medi-Cal. Managed-care-only services (Enhanced Care Management, Community Supports) do not continue in FFS.

changes.value: 1 month for the MAGI New Adult Group; 2 months for all other groups
changes.detail: Previously up to 3 months for everyone. Applies to applications with an application date of January 1, 2027 or later. To get retroactive coverage you must have met the work rule or qualified for an exemption in the retroactive month.

changes.item: July 1, 2027 — asset limits drop to the SSI-linked level
changes.value: $21,000 for one person, $31,000 for two, +$1,550 per additional person
changes.detail: Applies to the non-MAGI programs only.

changes.item: July 1, 2027 — dental coverage reduced for some members
changes.value: Full dental ends for some; emergency dental continues
changes.detail: "You will continue to get full dental benefits if you are: A child (ages 0-18); Pregnant (through pregnancy and up to one year after); Under age 26 and were in foster care on your 18th birthday."

changes.item: July 1, 2027 — monthly premiums for some members
changes.value: A monthly fee to keep full-scope Medi-Cal for some immigration statuses
changes.detail: Not required for children, pregnant people, or former foster youth under 26. If unpaid, coverage drops to restricted scope (emergency, pregnancy, nursing home care).

state-help.value: California kept covering immigrants regardless of status, and is now phasing that back
state-help.detail: The state-funded coverage that LPRs inside the five-year bar receive is the reason the 2026 freeze did not leave a coverage gap in California.
A state program that supplements — and does not replace — the federal premium tax credit, preserving $0-premium Silver plans up to 150% FPL and lowering premiums from 150% to 200% FPL.

state-help.value: Cover continued during the 30-day notice period, a data-conflict safeguard, and a hearing before any denial
state-help.detail: New in 2026: (1) the county must continue Medi-Cal during the 30-calendar-day notice-of-noncompliance period for members who otherwise qualify; (2) when reliable data sources conflict adversely, the county must ask the applicant to confirm before taking adverse action; (3) the county must check every other basis of eligibility, and must give written notice and a state hearing opportunity, before denying.

state-help.value: Notices mailed from late August 2026; work-rule insert in every application packet October–December 2026
state-help.detail: DHCS also runs a text-message campaign and points members to dhcs.ca.gov/workrules, and says it will send more information about local work, volunteer, job-training and school opportunities before the end of 2026.

state-help.value: DHCS may defer any change that lacks an appropriation
state-help.detail: WIC § 14005.69(r): if a change creates a fiscal impact requiring an additional appropriation that has not been made, "the department may defer implementation of the change until that additional appropriation is made." If it does so, DHCS must notify the fiscal and policy committees and publish the notice on its website. This is the mechanism by which individual parts of the 2027 changes could be delayed.
